bio: Founded two startups, sold one, buried the other. Now I mostly write about tech and work, minus the LinkedIn voice.
Writer. Small rituals, ordinary days, the things nobody tells you about adult life. Edinburgh via Kochi and Leicester.
Played in Spain's U-19s a long time ago. Now coaching kids in Leith and lifting heavy things slowly.
I cook for strangers on Thursday nights in Leith. Food, cities, and who gets a seat at the table.
Ex-astrophysicist, current explainer. I will tell you why the sky is doing that, whether you asked or not.
Lab tech. Writes about replication and small, unglamorous results.
UX researcher. I watch people use things and quietly despair. Osaka, then Glasgow, now Edinburgh.
Gaelic-medium primary teacher. From Lewis, homesick for weather that means it.
Junior doctor on an A&E rotation. Accra-born, Aberdeen-raised. Opinions are mine; the tiredness is collective.
I drive a city bus, mostly the night routes. You'd be amazed what people tell a bus driver.
Pizzaiolo from Naples, eleven years in Scotland. Dough is a living thing and so are my opinions.
Urban planner. Streets, housing, bikes, benches. Grew up between Casablanca and Lyon.
Plumber. Hibs till I die, which at this rate will be stress-related.
Data scientist. I build the models and then tell you not to trust them too much.
Payments engineer. Ask me why your card got declined abroad (I probably don't know either).
Staff nurse, nights. From Galway. Running on tea and gallows humour.
Climate scientist (ice cores). Swedish, so contractually obliged to have opinions about saunas.
Robotics PhD. My robot can open a door 60% of the time.
Chartered accountant by day, club cricketer by weekend. Glasgow born, Edinburgh tolerated.
Jiu-jitsu coach, part-time barista, full-time Brazilian about coffee.
Illustrator. Fringe veteran (4 shows, 2 audiences). Draws the city on the back of receipts.
Economist at a small policy institute. I like boring numbers and unpopular trade-offs.
Software tester from Kharkiv. I find bugs for a living and in everything else for free.
I run a hostel off the Cowgate. Every night is a different country.
Community pharmacist. Taiwanese-Scottish. Will gently ask if you've read the leaflet.
Brewer at a tiny place in Leith. Czech, so yes, I have views on lager.
Philosophy lecturer. Ethics, technology and the occasional argument with my own students.
PE teacher and lapsed flanker. Borders born. Rugby, mostly, and kids who hate cross-country.
Law student, tenants' union volunteer. Rent is the story of this city.
Yarn shop in Stockbridge. Hearts season ticket. I contain multitudes.
Indie game dev. Shipping a small game about lighthouses, eventually.
From Ohio, running Edinburgh's hills badly. Skeptical of anything sold as a 'protocol'.
Architect. Damascus, then Edinburgh. Stone, light, and buildings that age well.
Delivery rider, Celtic fan, part-time philosopher of the bike lane.
Actuary. I calculate how long things last, including my patience.
Startup ops from Guadalajara. Spreadsheets by day, tacos by obligation.
Retired civil engineer. Allotment in Inverleith. I write to the council so you don't have to.
Alto in a small early-music choir. Bulgarian, twelve years in Edinburgh.
Arable farmer, east Fife. Weather, soil, and the price of diesel.
Librarian at a branch library that keeps nearly closing.
Moss ecologist. From Rotorua, now permanently damp.
Night baker. I see the city at 4am. Rye, mostly.
PhD on medieval marginalia: the doodles, complaints and cats monks left in the margins.
Birds at Cramond and Musselburgh. Patience is a skill.
Retired maths teacher. Chess club on Tuesdays. Still marking things in my head.
Just moved from Porto Alegre for a master's in public health. Say hi?
Backend dev, here for the hackathon.
Dutch. Cycles everywhere. Still working out how this app works.
